cur:catacombs-lucina-good-shepherd-wilpe.summary: Within a painted circle, a young shepherd in a short belted tunic stands with a sheep across his shoulders while another animal stands at his feet, framed by slender plants. The image, among the oldest in the Crypt of Lucina, expresses in the simplest pastoral language the hope of the Christians buried here: that Christ, the Good Shepherd, would carry them home.
facts: The Crypt of Lucina is one of the earliest nuclei of the Catacomb of Callixtus on the Via Appia; Commons and Wilpert date its paintings to the late 2nd or early 3rd century.
This image is Wilpert's 1903 black-and-white photographic plate (pl. 35); the painting is distinct from the better-known coloured Good Shepherd with a milk pail in the same catacomb.
Painting reproduced from Joseph Wilpert, Die Malereien der Katakomben Roms (Freiburg, 1903), whose plates were photographed in the catacombs and in some cases hand-coloured.
cur:catacombs-lucina-good-shepherd-wilpe.notes: The ram-bearer (kriophoros) type was also used in pagan funerary art; in the Christian setting of the Crypt of Lucina it is generally read as Christ the Good Shepherd, though the identification is an interpretation of a symbolic image.
